strokeOrder: draw the upper bar from left to right
lift, draw the lower bar from left to right
lift, begin above the upper bar and run the long diagonal down and right through both bars, then without lifting turn sharply and hook back to the left
lift, begin at the upper left of the curve, drop down and finish along the base to the right
lift, draw the left tick of the dakuten down to the right
lift, draw the right tick down to the right
strokeOrderNote: KanjiVG's 0304e file records ぎ as six stroke paths in this order and direction: き's four strokes (the upper bar, the lower bar, the long diagonal with its hook and the curve at the foot), then the dakuten's two ticks, the left one first, each drawn down to the right; so there are five pen lifts.

strokeOrderSource.citation: KanjiVG, kanji/0304e.svg, hiragana ぎ (U+304E HIRAGANA LETTER GI), six stroke paths kvg:0304e-s1 to s6 (Ulrich Apel and contributors, CC BY-SA 3.0)
strokeOrderSource.variation: KanjiVG stores each stroke as one directed path in writing order: s1 to s4 are き's strokes, the same paths as in its file for き, kanji/0304d.svg; s5 and s6 are the dakuten, the left tick first and then the right one, each drawn down to the right. Only the order and direction are taken from that file. The learner path's coordinates are the bundled Noto Sans JP outline's own medial line, so the print glyph's proportions, not KanjiVG's handwriting-style ones, decide where each stroke runs. Some hands join the hook to the curve below it; KanjiVG and the bundled print glyph keep them apart, and so does this book.

notes: き voiced. Opens ぎんこう, a bank; with it the book writes the whole voiced k row, が ぎ ぐ げ ご.
